enterprise.tenants: multi-tenant with tenant roles (tenant-admin, editor, viewer); the host is the first tenant at deploy
enterprise.users: the first user is the deployer's account, a super admin; API keys per user for MCP clients

access.create: a call by anyone (its address folds the call); other kinds by a super admin, a tenant-admin or editor of the entry's tenant, or the tenant's writer token
access.update: no one: an entry is its content address, so a change is a new entry
access.delete: a super admin, a tenant-admin of the entry's tenant (a where on the tenant), or the tenant's admin token

enterprise.signing: ML-DSA at the edge (seal), the gate verifying
enterprise.realtime: 5 streams and the collision precondition by address
enterprise.ui: MCP Apps views and the shadcn registry
enterprise.gate: the e2e repetition code over every host

licence.description: commercial use of the QPU framework on one named domain, for a year

price.says: 475.00 USD per domain per year, the catalogue's amount in the host's currency

order.checkout: /checkout: the ecommerce plugin's own, the Stripe adapter the payment
order.then: on payment the licence entry is granted to the tenant (the billing toolbox's licence ledger) and the bundle is the tenant's to deploy from site/ (npx wrangler deploy, OpenNext); the status streams requested → generated → paid → deployed

usable.inUi: the request is a submission of the form-builder's form "Request an app" (seeded); its afterChange hook generates this answer into the media collection as a JSON file; the tenant's settings (its tenants document) are the plugin options merged into every qpu block call under its hosts; nothing added to the schema
usable.viaMcp: the Payload MCP plugin serves the installed plugins' default collections: a client requests (a form submission), reads the bundle (media), buys the licence (a product in a cart at the checkout) and configures (tenants.settings) with its API key
usable.asPlugin: a tenant-configurable plugin: the same generated app, configured per tenant as data in the plugins' own collections, never a second Payload config and never a collection added

monetises: the QPU is paid for the apps it generates on request: the Apps collection in the Payload UI takes the request, this answer is the app, the catalogue prices it, the ecommerce plugin sells it, and the tenant uses it in the same UI or through the Payload MCP plugin

bundleFiles.site/README.qpu.md:
# QPU full stack

The source of payloadcms.com (MIT) is the full stack, forked under site/: its 12 collections, 30 blocks, 5 globals and 10 fields kept. Applied: `src/blocks/Qpu/config.ts` (the qpu block, the shape every tools/call result carries in _meta.payload), registered in payload.config blocks and the pages layout; `src/components/blocks/Qpu/index.tsx` (the renderer: the page asks the Worker for the block and carries its widget), mapped in RenderBlocks; `src/payload.qpu.config.ts` (search and multi-tenant beside the site's four plugins, the database the RAID); `src/collections/Tenants.ts` (the multi-tenant plugin's own collection: the hosts that name the tenants). The catch-all makes prefixes useless: a UUID is one address — the entry's JSON when the client accepts application/json (the entries collection's own door), the block's page otherwise; the list is /api/entries; /mcp is the MCP plugin's /api/mcp and /.well-known/qpu.json the endpoint /api/qpu; no Worker behind any of them. Deploy at Cloudflare beside this Worker; every step at whole uptime: configure { kind: 'migration' }.

# @uuidna/qpu: the names the full stack binds to, by provider (values never travel; set them in the provider's dashboard or .env)
# GENERATED by npm run next through configure { kind: 'bindings' }; edit src/quantum/toolboxes/payload.ts (BINDINGS), never this file.

# cloudflare: the Worker and the docket (until the gate decodes the Payload app beside them)
#   free: 100k requests a day, static assets free; paid for: requests beyond the tier, Durable Object requests and storage; kept free: ETag involutions answer 304 without a body; a block computed once is teleported, never recomputed
QPU_WRITE_TOKEN_UUIDNA=
QPU_WRITE_TOKEN_PSG=
QPU_WRITE_TOKEN_CECI=
QPU_ADMIN_TOKEN_UUIDNA=
QPU_ADMIN_TOKEN_PSG=
QPU_ADMIN_TOKEN_CECI=
QPU_DATA_KEY=
QPU_SIGNING_KEY_UUIDNA=
QPU_SIGNING_KEY_PSG=
QPU_SIGNING_KEY_CECI=
QPU_MCP_HOSTS_UUIDNA=
QPU_MCP_HOSTS_PSG=
QPU_MCP_HOSTS_CECI=

# mongodb-atlas: the database behind Payload (the docket over the mongo language)
#   free: M0 shared cluster, 512 MB; paid for: storage and operations beyond M0; kept free: content-addressed entries are written once; reads come from the app's cache by tag
DATABASE_URI=

# vercel: the Payload app (Next.js) and blob storage
#   free: hobby: serverless functions, 100 GB bandwidth, blob 1 GB; paid for: function invocations and bandwidth beyond hobby; kept free: tags revalidate one page per change; UUID pages are immutable and cached forever
PAYLOAD_SECRET=
BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN=
BLOB_STORAGE_ENABLED=
BLOB_STORE_ID=
NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL=
NEXT_PRIVATE_REVALIDATION_KEY=
NEXT_PRIVATE_DRAFT_SECRET=
QPU_ORIGIN=

# stripe: the licence checkout per tenant (the Worker) and the ecommerce plugin's payment (the app)
#   free: no fee without a payment; paid for: a fee per successful payment; kept free: a plan is computed here; Stripe is asked only at checkout
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_UUIDNA=
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_PSG=
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_CECI=
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET_UUIDNA=
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET_PSG=
STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET_CECI=
STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=
NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=
STRIPE_WEBHOOKS_SIGNING_SECRET=

# payload-mcp: the handler's tools served by @payloadcms/plugin-mcp
#   free: the app's own compute; paid for: nothing beyond the app; kept free: tools/call is pure: the same arguments answer the same address
PAYLOAD_MCP_API_KEY=

# anthropic: the operator agent that mounts the QPU through the MCP connector (only when named)
#   free: none; paid for: tokens of every request; kept free: never called by the tree; the registration is computed, the request is the operator's
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
